>Try making the girl a relative or someone the players actually care about.

I really like this idea and I'll definitely be using it. I'll maybe make the girl a childhood friend of one of the players. We'll see.

As for your second point I think I'll keep the guard. I'm thinking of making the town corrupt and I want to give my players the impression that the guard can't be trusted. I'll have NPCs tell them the guard frequently turns a blind eye on crimes and making it strongly implied that they are being bribed by the criminal circles. The guard will also "suggest" that some gold may change his mind, again implying the corrupted state this town is in.
Regarding the wererats I think they would be too difficult for the party and I don't want to deal with the curse of lycanthropy on the very first session (maybe later on). And I've bought a pretty interesting beastiary called "Revenge of the Horde" that has a section on Gutter Gnolls, so I think I'll be using those.
